notes:
CIRCUIT: single-node-pair ladder. A 30A I-DC source on the left feeds a top rail; the 9F capacitor sits in series in that top rail; a 16ohm resistor hangs from the middle of the top rail down to the bottom (ground) rail; further right a 3kV V-DC sits in series in the top rail and feeds a 5mH inductor down to the same bottom rail. The bottom rail ties I-DC bottom, resistor bottom, GND and inductor bottom together. 6 components, 4 nets.

NET MAP:
  n1 = left vertical rail: top terminal of I-DC #4 (229,427) up to y~348 and right along the top rail to the LEFT plate of capacitor #0 (294,348).
  n2 = top-middle rail: RIGHT plate of capacitor #0 (369,349) -> east along y~350 through site S4 (481,350) -> top lead of resistor #2 (483,392) and onward east to the LEFT terminal of V-DC #1 (579,351).
  n3 = top-right rail: RIGHT terminal of V-DC #1 (674,356) east to x~727 then down to top lead of inductor #3 (721,399).
  0  = bottom rail at y~570: bottom of I-DC #4 (223,517), bottom of resistor #2 (482,500) down through site S6 (476,572), GND #5 stub (477,575), and east to bottom of inductor #3 (727,522).

PORT FIXES (both were the classic 'terminal landed on the handwritten value label' error, each producing a 1-terminal net):
  - Capacitor #0 t0 was bound to p1@(319,314), which is a stroke of the handwritten '9F' label sitting ABOVE the top rail, not a lead (p2@(344,310) is the same label). Re-bound t0 -> p3@(294,348), the real left plate lead (wire 151), which is the same wire run as I-DC #4 top. This removed the orphan net n1 and merged the capacitor's left plate with the I-DC top as the drawing shows.
  - V-DC #1 t1 was bound to p1@(652,315), a stroke of the handwritten '3kV' label above the source. Re-bound t1 -> p2@(674,356), the real right lead (wire 86), which is the same wire run as inductor #3 top. This removed orphan nets n3/n4.
  - Resistor #2 had a third port candidate p2@(519,442) which is the '16ohm' label brushing the box; the tracer had already NOT used it (t0=p1 top, t1=p0 bottom), which is correct - left as is.

JUDGEMENT CALLS / SITES:
  - S4 (481,350) deg=3, CRITICAL, dot=1.8, hop=0.0: JUNCTION. The 5x crop shows a clean T - the resistor's top lead runs up and terminates on the horizontal top rail, it does not continue above it. A T is a junction by definition; there is no fourth branch, so 'crossing' is not even expressible here. The alternative ('none') would strand the resistor's top lead on a one-terminal net and leave the 16ohm resistor with no path to the source, i.e. electrically impossible. Confirmed junction.
  - S6 (476,572) deg=3, CRITICAL, dot=1.4, hop=0.0: JUNCTION. The crop shows the resistor's descending lead terminating on the horizontal bottom rail with the GND symbol drawn immediately below on the same stroke - a T plus the ground stub. Reading it as anything but a junction would either leave the resistor bottom floating or split the bottom rail, disconnecting the I-DC return path from ground. Confirmed junction.
  - S0 (325,298) and S1 (342,300): NOT critical - these are self-intersections of the handwritten '9F' glyph (the crossbar of the 'F' meeting its stem) sitting above the top rail. Left at the default; they touch no component terminal after the port fix.
  - S2 (650,306) and S3 (657,306): NOT critical - self-intersections of the handwritten '3kV' glyph above the V-DC. Left at the default; after re-binding V-DC t1 to the real lead these are electrically inert.
  - No solder dots anywhere on this sheet and no hops/jogs; every wire meeting is a plain T, so there was no dot-vs-hop ambiguity to resolve.

CLASSES: all six symbols match their labels - two parallel plates = Capacitor (9F), circle with '+ -' = V-DC (3kV), zigzag = Resistor (16ohm), coil loops = Inductor (5mH), circle with an arrow = I-DC (30A), stacked shrinking bars = GND. No re-classification needed.

UNRESOLVED: nothing. All 5 gap bridges were inert (the summary reports 0 change the netlist) and were left alone. ERC clean with 4 nets, every net has >=2 terminals.
